newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil blocks hike in steel, drug prices - papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil blocks hike in steel, drug prices - papers.

text.p: Brazil's government has ordered three major steelmakers to suspend an increase in steel prices that the companies had planned to impelement between June 27 and July 1, Brazilian newspapers said Friday.
Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said Cosipa, CSN and Usiminas would each have to pay a 45,000 reais daily fine if they did not suspend the planned price hikes of between four and 12 percent.
The government has also ordered pharmaceutical group Hoechst Marion Roussell, a unit of Hoechst AG, to revoke recent increases in drug prices which were above 100 percent, O Globo daily said.

The measures are part of the government's decision to open a probe into the steel, pharmaceutical and aluminum sectors to investigate allegations that the companies had formed cartels to fix prices, a wide range of Brazilian newspapers reported.

The decision to investigate those sectors also come one day after Brazil's anti-trust body ordered brewers Brahma and Miller Brewing Co to dissolver their joint-venture within 24 months because it was found to impede competition.
